sources.entry: DVinyl ⚠ - Modern collection manager for physical media (vinyls, CDs, cassettes, books, movies, and video games). MIT Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: DVinyl is a self-hostable, plugin-based collection manager for physical media such as vinyls, CDs, books, movies, video games, LEGO sets and board games.
summary.what_it_does: It runs on your own server and pulls cover art and metadata from databases including Discogs, Hardcover, Open Library, TMDB, IGDB, ScreenScraper, Rebrickable and BoardGameGeek. Each media type is a plugin that can be enabled or disabled per collection from the admin panel, and new types can be added through a no-code plugin editor or a code plugin. It offers grid, table and virtual shelf views, lists and playlists, multiple collections, and barcode scanning with the camera or bulk import from Discogs and Goodreads. It also includes market value estimates with price history for music, game completion times from IGDB, printable QR/barcode labels, and a wishlist. Sharing features include user roles (admin, editor, viewer), optional OIDC SSO, and read-only public share links. The README also describes optional bring-your-own-key AI assist for import and plugin drafting.
use_cases: catalog a vinyl or CD collection
track physical movie and game collections
manage a board game or LEGO set inventory
estimate the value of a record collection
generate printable barcode labels for media
share a read-only collection view with others
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml (the Docker guide has the full file)
Set environment variables in a .env file (see API keys guide)
Or run 'make docker-up' if make is installed
Open the web UI in your browser and finish setup
On ZimaOS/CasaOS, install DVinyl from the TwoBytes Store; on Unraid, use the Community Applications template
notable: Plugin-based architecture: each media type is a plugin, and users can add their own without changing the core
No-code plugin editor for creating manual collection types with custom fields, formats, icons and colors
Market value estimates and price history charts for music collections
Public read-only share links or QR codes, optionally limited to part of a collection
Multilingual interface (English, French, German, Spanish, Italian) with 14 color themes
caveats: The author says this is their first app of this kind and parts of the frontend and comments were AI-generated, so backend errors may exist
Requires API keys from several metadata providers for full functionality (per the API keys guide)
Built-in AI features require the user to supply their own AI key
